title: Fender CEO tries to clear up his controversial AI comments.
description:
Bud Cole has been catching some flak over comments he made to T3 about AI’s role in music. Now he’s attempting to clarify what he meant. You can read his full statement provided to The Verge at the bottom of our post from this weekend, but here’s the gist:
> If AI has a role, it should only be as a tool that helps beginners learn and gives seasoned artists new ways to explore, refine and experiment with their own creative ideas. If it can help a beginner understand a difficult chord or practice one more day instead of putting the guitar back in its case, then that’s something worth exploring. But let me be clear: every creative idea starts with people, and music starts and ends with people. It always will.
[Link: Fender’s CEO seems to think your bandmates are just analog AI | https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/974265/fender-ceo-bud-cole-ai-music | The Verge]

title: Thomson Reuters lifts full-year revenue forecast with focus on AI rollout
description: Thomson Reuters has revised its full-year organic revenue outlook, now anticipating an increase of around eight percent. The company witnessed a remarkable nine percent revenue growth in the second quarter, achieving $1.95 billion. Excluding certain items, earnings per share rose to ninety-nine cents, exceeding market predictions. CEO Steve Hasker highlighted the company's commitment to substantial investment in artificial intelligence, aiming to boost product offerings and explore innovative commercialization pathways.

title: US stock futures edge higher and oil resumes ascent
description: U.S. stock futures edged higher Wednesday morning, helped by strong corporate earnings reports and hopes for a deal setting the stage for talks that might eventually end the fighting in Iran. Dow Jones Industrial Average futures rose 0.3%, while S&P 500 futures added 0.4%. Nasdaq futures gained 0.2%. The Walt Disney Co. reported results that beat analyst expectations, helped by “Toy Story 5.” SpaceX shares tumbled despite a surge in revenue as the company boosted its spending on artificial intelligence.
